`npm run typecheck` passed in the deterministic wrapper and the diff is lane-scoped, but the package update restart path is not safe to merge yet.
Blocking: `executeControlPlanePackageUpdate` runs restart commands before the bridge reports job completion. In `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-package-update.ts:10-15`, `runPackageUpdateRestartCommands` is called inside the update execution, and `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:150-184` only POSTs `/complete` after that returns. A real `controlBridgeRestartCommand` such as a pm2/systemd restart can terminate the current bridge process before it reaches `/complete`, leaving the job stuck as claimed and failing the acceptance requirement to complete with structured result data. Defer/detach the bridge self-restart until after the status and job completion are posted, or otherwise make completion durable before restarting the current process. Add focused coverage for this ordering; the current restart test uses a harmless child command and does not cover the self-restart hazard.

`npm run typecheck` passed in the deterministic wrapper and the diff is lane-scoped, but the round-1 blocker is still present. The package update path still executes restart commands before the bridge posts the updated status and `/complete` result, so a real bridge self-restart can terminate the current bridge process and leave the job stuck as claimed.
Blocking: `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-package-update.ts:10` calls `runPackageUpdateRestartCommands` inside `executeControlPlanePackageUpdate`, and `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:150` only posts repo status and `/complete` after that function returns. Defer or detach `controlBridgeRestartCommand` until after the status update and job completion are durably posted, or otherwise make completion durable before restarting the current bridge process.
Missing focused verification: `tests/unit/control-plane-package-update-bridge.test.ts:109` uses a harmless child process restart command, so it proves command execution but not the self-restart ordering hazard. Add coverage that asserts job completion/status reporting happens before any bridge self-restart command can stop the running bridge.

`npm run typecheck` passed in the deterministic wrapper and the diff remains lane-scoped, but the prior blocking restart-ordering issue is still present, so this is not safe to merge.
Blocking: `executeControlPlanePackageUpdate` still runs restart commands before the bridge posts the updated repo status and `/complete` result. `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-package-update.ts:10-15` calls `runPackageUpdateRestartCommands`, while `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:150-184` only posts status and completes the job after that call returns. A real `controlBridgeRestartCommand` can terminate/restart the running bridge before completion is durably reported, leaving the job stuck as claimed and violating the package update completion requirement. Defer/detach the bridge self-restart until after status and job completion are posted, or otherwise make completion durable before restarting the current bridge process.
Missing focused verification: `tests/unit/control-plane-package-update-bridge.test.ts:109-124` still uses harmless child-process commands, so it verifies command execution but not the self-restart ordering hazard. Add coverage that proves status reporting and job completion occur before any bridge restart command that could stop the active bridge process.

`npm run typecheck` passed in the deterministic wrapper, and the bridge restart is now deferred past the normal success path. Still blocking: the deferred self-restart is not tied to durable job completion, so the prior stuck-claimed-job failure mode can still happen on `/complete` failures.
In `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:173`, deferred bridge restart commands are queued before the job completion request. The completion POST at `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:199` is swallowed with `.catch(() => null)`, but the deferred restart still runs at `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:256`. If `/api/jobs/:id/complete` fails transiently, the bridge can restart itself while the job remains claimed, violating the package update completion requirement. Only launch deferred self-restart after completion is durably acknowledged, or drop the deferred restart and surface a failure when completion cannot be posted.
The focused deferral test in `tests/unit/control-plane-package-update-bridge.test.ts:109` covers the successful completion ordering, but it does not cover the completion-failure path. Add coverage proving a configured `controlBridgeRestartCommand` is not launched when `/complete` fails or cannot be acknowledged.

`npm run typecheck` passed and the branch appears mergeable, but the default restart helper can report success even when a relaunched service immediately exits. That leaves the job history saying `restarted` while the server or bridge is actually down, so the relaunch-failure acceptance criteria are not satisfied.
Blocking: `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-restart-helper.ts:230` resolves a relaunch as `restarted` on the child `spawn` event and never observes early process exit or service readiness. A command such as `node missing-script.js`, a bad cwd/env, or a server bind failure can spawn successfully and then exit immediately, but the helper records `status: 'restarted'` at `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-restart-helper.ts:232-238`. Update the helper to detect immediate relaunch failure/readiness before recording success, and add focused coverage for a process that spawns and exits non-zero after spawn.

`npm run typecheck` passed and the diff is in scope, but the prior relaunch-failure blocker remains. The default restart helper still records a service as `restarted` as soon as Node emits `spawn`, so a process that starts and immediately exits can leave job history reporting success while the service is down.
Blocking: `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-restart-helper.ts:230` settles `relaunchService` with `status: 'restarted'` on the child `spawn` event and never waits for early exit, readiness, heartbeat, or PID liveness after launch. A command such as `node missing-script.js`, a bad cwd/env, or a bind failure can spawn and then exit non-zero, but the helper will still record `restarted`, so relaunch failure cases are not reported clearly. Update the helper to detect immediate post-spawn failure/readiness before recording success, and add focused coverage for a restart command that spawns successfully then exits non-zero; the current new test only covers an ENOENT spawn error at `tests/unit/control-plane-default-restart.test.ts:193`.

`npm run typecheck` passed, and the diff is in scope and merge-tree did not show conflicts with `origin/dev`. However the PR branch HEAD still has the prior relaunch-failure bug; the apparent fix is only present as unstaged local changes, so it is not safely mergeable as reviewed.

A command that spawns and then fails can still leave job history reporting success while the service is down.
Blocking verification gap in committed `tests/unit/control-plane-default-restart.test.ts`: the branch only covers an ENOENT spawn error, not a process that successfully spawns and exits non-zero. The unstaged local test/fix should be included in the branch, or equivalent committed coverage added, before approval.

`npm run typecheck` passed and the prior early-exit relaunch failure blocker is now covered in the committed helper/test. However, the default restart outcome can still be lost from job history because the helper records results only after relaunching the bridge, while the relaunched bridge can cause the new server process to cache and rewrite stale control-plane state first.
Blocking: `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-restart-helper.ts:89` relaunches all stopped targets, including `controlBridge`, before `recordRestartOutcome(...)` runs at `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-restart-helper.ts:108`. A relaunched bridge immediately polls in `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-bridge.ts:331-333`, which can make the newly relaunched server load `.autonomy/control-plane/state.json` before the helper writes the final `restarted`/`relaunch-failed` result. Because `loadControlPlaneState` caches state per process at `src/server/control-plane/control-plane-store.ts:42-53`, later server writes can preserve or overwrite the stale `deferred` restart result, so restart outcomes may not be visible in the control panel job history. Update the flow so helper results cannot race with the new server/bridge state cache, and add focused coverage for this cross-process stale-state/job-history case.

tasks.title: Review [architecture-agent] Implement Approved PR Merge Watchdog
tasks.description: Review pr-prd-approved-pr-merge-watchdog-5461cc-architecture-agent for Address review for [architecture-agent] Implement Approved PR Merge Watchdog
acceptance: Detect PRs in approved state that have not merged after a short timeout.

required status checks
branch protection
conflicts
and stale branch state.

Blocking issue found. `npm run typecheck` passed, and the branch appears scoped, but the watchdog can merge a PR whose head changed after approval.
`src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog.ts:61` attempts an automatic merge whenever GitHub diagnosis says `canMerge`, but neither candidate selection nor diagnosis compares the current PR commit count/head with `reviewTask.reviewedCommitCount`. `diagnoseApprovedPullRequestMerge` refreshes the remote commit count at `src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog-diagnosis.ts:245`, so a new commit pushed after approval can still be auto-merged if GitHub allows it. Existing reviewer retry logic guards this at `src/agents/ReviewAgentDefinition.ts:560`. The watchdog should reuse that stale-review guard and surface a clear stale/unreviewed-head blocker or requeue review, with a focused test covering commitCount > reviewedCommitCount.

Blocking issue remains from round 1. The deterministic `npm run typecheck` check passed and the diff is lane-scoped, but the watchdog can still auto-merge a PR whose head changed after approval.
`src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog.ts:61` attempts the merge whenever diagnosis reports `canMerge`, and candidate selection at `src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog.ts:139` still treats the PR as approved if `pr.status` or the latest review is approved. `diagnoseApprovedPullRequestMerge` refreshes the remote commit count at `src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog-diagnosis.ts:245`; meanwhile sync can detect stale reviewed commits at `src/sync/derived-pr.ts:291` but leaves the PR approved, so the watchdog can merge before the requeued review runs. Add the same stale-review guard used by reviewer retry logic: block/requeue when current commit count or head is newer than `reviewTask.reviewedCommitCount`, surface a clear stale/unreviewed-head merge reason, and add a focused test covering `commitCount > reviewedCommitCount`.

Blocking issue remains. The deterministic `npm run typecheck` check passed, but the watchdog can still auto-merge an approved PR after new commits are pushed beyond the reviewed head.
`src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog.ts:61` attempts the merge whenever diagnosis reports `canMerge`, while candidate selection/approval checks at `src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog.ts:114` and `src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog.ts:139` never compare the current PR commit count/head with `reviewTask.reviewedCommitCount`. Diagnosis refreshes the remote commit count at `src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog-diagnosis.ts:245`, and the merge command's `evaluateMerge` path only checks approved status/latest review at `src/autonomy-v2/commands/shared-repo.ts:306`. Add a stale-review guard before automatic merge, surface a clear stale/unreviewed-head blocker or requeue review, and add focused coverage for `commitCount > reviewedCommitCount`.

`npm run typecheck` passes and the stale-reviewed-head guard is now present, but the branch is not safe to approve or merge yet.
Merge safety blocker: the lane still records pending follow-up work for this same PR. `prompts/autonomous/v2/queues/architecture-agent.json:1086` has follow-up 2 active and `prompts/autonomous/v2/queues/architecture-agent.json:1109` has follow-up 3 queued. The merge command blocks when any lane task or `pendingTaskIds` remain pending (`src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge.ts:23`, `src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge.ts:30`). Complete or clear those stale follow-up tasks so the PR has no pending lane work, then rerun `npm run typecheck`.
Duplicate merge-attempt risk: the scheduler runs `runApprovedPrMergeWatchdog` before acquiring the state lock (`src/server/orchestrator/scheduler.ts:51`, lock starts at `src/server/orchestrator/scheduler.ts:63`), and the watchdog only records attempt state after a failed merge attempt (`src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog.ts:81`, `src/autonomy-v2/commands/merge-watchdog.ts:87`). Concurrent ticks can select the same approved PR and issue duplicate merge attempts before either writes `lastAttemptKey`. Make candidate selection/attempt marking atomic under the state lock, or otherwise record an in-flight attempt before executing the merge, with focused coverage for duplicate-run idempotency.
